lines.text: Birthday [Verjaardag]: for Dutch children the birthday is the most important day of the year.
They get presents, there is a cake with candles [taart met kaarsjes] and the visitors sing the Dutch birthday song ['Lang zal ze leven'].
Children may bring a treat [trakteren] for the class at school.
Many adults also celebrate their birthday every year, often on a weekend day.
Family and friends bring a small gift and eat cake.
Can't come?
Then you can congratulate [feliciteren] the birthday person with a phone call, a card or a message.
Wedding [Bruiloft]: when people are getting married, they first send a card with an invitation [uitnodiging].
Usually the woman wears a white dress [witte jurk] and the man a nice suit [kostuum].
They marry at the town hall [gemeentehuis] and sometimes also in church.
In the evening there is often a party.
In the Netherlands two men or two women [twee mannen of twee vrouwen] can also marry each other.
Many people do not want to marry but to live together unmarried [samenwonen].
A baby is born: in the Netherlands babies are sometimes born not in the hospital but at home [thuis] — if everything goes well, the parents may choose this themselves.
The parents send an announcement card [kaartje].
If you want to visit, you usually have to make an appointment first.
Visitors are served Dutch rusk with aniseed sprinkles [beschuit met muisjes].
Someone has passed an exam: whoever passes an exam receives a diploma.
Often they hang out a flag with their school bag [vlag met zijn schooltas] on it outside and throw a party.
Someone has died: the family sends a card to family, friends and acquaintances [kennissen].
The card says where and when the burial [begrafenis] or the cremation [crematie] is.
People gather, a few people say something about the deceased person and there is music.
The coffin [kist] is present, often with flowers.
What do you say when?
My condolences ['Gecondoleerd'] is what you say to the family when someone has died; you can also say be strong / much strength ['Veel sterkte'].
Congratulations ['Gefeliciteerd'] is what you say when people are happy: on a birthday, when a baby is born, at a wedding, or when someone has passed an exam.
